summary.name: Are site reliability engineers the next data scientists?
summary.one_liner: A 2016 TechCrunch opinion essay arguing that site reliability engineering (SRE) practices from large Internet companies will spread to enterprise IT, with Rocana Ops cited as an example product.
use_cases: Understanding why site reliability engineering is growing in enterprise IT
Finding out how large Internet companies organize operations
Evaluating big data tools for IT monitoring and root cause analysis
Planning how an IT team could adopt SRE practices
Reading background on containers, cluster schedulers and microservices adoption
summary.what_it_does: The essay traces how technologies such as containers, Kubernetes, Mesos, Hadoop and microservices came out of large Internet companies like Google, Amazon and Netflix and spread into general industry. It describes site reliability engineering as an operations discipline staffed by software engineers, citing Google's SRE team growing to more than 1,000 engineers. It then gives a hypothetical e-commerce example in which logs and telemetry are collected centrally and machine learning flags anomalies such as mobile request timeouts. The author presents Rocana Ops, a commercial product, as a packaged way to bring SRE-style root cause analysis to enterprise teams, and disclosed that he is an investor in Rocana. The piece ends with recommendations for IT teams to weigh people and process alongside software.
notable: Opinion piece by an investor in Rocana, which it discloses
Describes Google's SRE team growing from a handful of engineers to more than 1,000
Hypothetical e-commerce troubleshooting walkthrough using ML anomaly detection
caveats: Opinion piece with a disclosed financial interest in the featured product (Rocana Ops)
Pricing, platform support and product details for Rocana Ops are not given on the page
